item.summary: Did anything notable happen this week? Not that I can remember. The weather was quite rainy - will that do? I'm just being silly, of course. We've had - and I suppose are still having - an historic week in video games, as Grand Theft Auto 6 arrives. It's dominated everything and I fear it's going to dominate this article too. But a reminder: next week is our "Not-GTA Week", so we'll be making a concerted effort to talk about games, probably smaller games, that aren't Godzilla blockbusters. Read more

item.title: How a $6 Beer in GTA 6 Sent Me Into a Spiral of Crime and Anxiety
item.summary: I'm relationship-maxxing GTA 6. Forget the money, the cars, or building a criminal empire. My main aim is to make Jason and Lucia so disgustingly loved up that NPCs violently vomit as we walk past being all cute together. I want them to be the perfect couple. I want romance. I want devotion. I want the sort of relationship that makes everyone else in Vice City feel deeply inadequate. Unfortunately, the nuanced way GTA 6 tracks even the smallest actions has turned me into a paranoid lunatic, constantly worrying that one wrong move will destroy my carefully cultivated romance. Case in point: a $6 beer that sent me into a cascade of disasters, petty crime, and emotional turmoil, eventually…

item.title: I've never known a moment like this in video games
item.summary: It was hard not to spend the first hour or so of Grand Theft Auto 6 's launch day in a kind of stun-lock. As far as video games editorial goes - which is not that far, in fairness; prepare for an over-flattering analogy - the effect was roughly the equivalent of Tom Hanks' experience, as his John H. Miller first set foot on Omaha beach. Tweets and reels whistled overhead, news leads stung the ears, exploding search terms blew apart some poor guides team ally on one side, while new discoveries in the early game - made by the millions and millions of launch-day players all picking it apart at once - appeared by surprise like some flanking ambush on the other. Read more
